# ET-HINTS-FULL (I): the hedging hump (FACT round 40 #4, paper 148, theorem T7)

Continuation of `Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers` (round 39 #5).  There the hint posterior was
uniform inside and outside the window.  Here the hint is *prior-proportional*: an oracle names a
set `S` of cells and the searcher trusts it at level `α`, i.e. puts mass `α` on `S` and `1 - α`
on its complement, each spread proportionally to the prior `p`:

  `trustPost p S α j = (α / P(S)) p j`  for `j ∈ S`,   `((1-α)/(1-P(S))) p j` otherwise.

At the calibrated trust `α = P(S)` the posterior *is* the prior (`trustPost_calibrated`).  The
Bayes-optimal expected number of probes `E_opt(α) = trustCost p S α` is studied as a function of
the trust level.

## Main results
* `trustPost_affine`, `trustPost_sum` — the trust family is an affine line of probability vectors.
* **`trustCost_concave`**, `trustCost_eq_inf_affine` — `E_opt` is concave and is the minimum of the
  `n!` affine functions `α ↦ probeCost (trustPost α) σ`: concave piecewise-linear (T7, shape).
* `optCost_le_uniform_level`, **`trustCost_le_uniform_level`** — no posterior whatsoever costs more
  than the uniform level `(n+1)/2`: this is the absolute ceiling of any hump.
* `hintPosterior_peak` — in the round-39 uniform-given-hit family the hump reaches this ceiling
  exactly, at `α = W/M`.
* **`hedging_hump`** — for *every* strictly decreasing prior and *every* window whose conditional
  mean position differs from the complement's, some intermediate trust `α ∈ (0,1)` makes the
  Bayes-optimal search strictly MORE expensive than ignoring the hint (`E_opt(α) > E_opt(P(S))`).
* **`minLaw_right_hump`** — under the min-law prior `J = min(p, q)` and a right-placed window of
  width `W ≤ M/3`, partial trust is strictly worse than no hint, than full trust (`α = 1`) and
  than full distrust (`α = 0`): partial trust is the most expensive regime.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Stage 1): (H1) `E_opt(α)` is concave piecewise-linear; (H2) intermediate trust can be
  worse than *both* endpoints *and* than no hint; (H3) the hump is a min-law accident.
Experiment (Stage 2): exact rational evaluation (sorted posterior, `α` grid step `1/200`), min-law,
  `M = 512` (blind `171.17`): right `x = 1/4` peak `196.50` at `α = 0.22` (reported `196.09`);
  right `x = 1/2` `197.84`; left `x = 1/4` `186.37` at `α = 0.31`; centered `x = 1/4` `176.97`;
  right `x = 1/64` `173.76`.  Every placement shows a hump.  `M = 256`: blind `85.83`, right
  `x = 1/4` peak `98.50`.
Analysis (Stage 3): (H1) true for any prior (minimum of affine functions).  (H2) true, and
  (H3) false: the hump is universal for strictly decreasing priors — at the calibrated trust the
  greedy order is rigid, so `E_opt` is locally the *linear* committed cost, whose slope is the
  difference of the two conditional mean positions; moving trust in the uphill direction
  strictly raises the cost.  For left windows the hump sits *below* the calibrated trust.
Critique (Stage 4): the hump never exceeds `(n+1)/2` (`trustCost_le_uniform_level`, `256.5` at
  `M = 512`), so "196 vs 171" is about 29% of the way to that ceiling.  The endpoint comparison
  needs a narrow window (`3W ≤ M`); for `x = 1/2` left/right the peak still exceeds both
  endpoints numerically but this is not covered.
-/
import Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers

namespace IntervalHintsHedgingHump

open Finset Filter Topology IntervalHintsTwoNumbers

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## 1. The trust family -/

/-- Prior mass of the hinted set `S`. -/
noncomputable def windowMass (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ := ∑ j ∈ S, p j

/-- Posterior after trusting the hint "`J ∈ S`" at level `α` (prior-proportional inside and
outside `S`). -/
noncomputable def trustPost (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) (j : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  (if j ∈ S then α / windowMass p S else (1 - α) / (1 - windowMass p S)) * p j

/-- Bayes-optimal expected number of probes at trust level `α`. -/
noncomputable def trustCost (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  optCost (trustPost p S α)

/-- At the calibrated trust `α = P(S)` the posterior is the prior. -/
theorem trustPost_calibrated (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0)
    (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) : trustPost p S (windowMass p S) = p := by
  have h1' : 1 - windowMass p S ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm h1)
  ext j
  unfold trustPost
  split_ifs
  · rw [div_self h0, one_mul]
  · rw [div_self h1', one_mul]

/-- The trust family is an affine line. -/
theorem trustPost_affine (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α β t : ℝ) :
    trustPost p S (t * α + (1 - t) * β) =
      fun j => t * trustPost p S α j + (1 - t) * trustPost p S β j := by
  ext j
  unfold trustPost
  split_ifs <;> ring

lemma sum_split_ite (S : Finset (Fin n)) (a b : ℝ) (f : Fin n → ℝ) :
    ∑ j, (if j ∈ S then a else b) * f j = a * ∑ j ∈ S, f j + b * ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, f j := by
  rw [← sum_add_sum_compl S, mul_sum, mul_sum]
  congr 1
  · exact sum_congr rfl fun j hj => by rw [if_pos hj]
  · exact sum_congr rfl fun j hj => by rw [if_neg (mem_compl.mp hj)]

/-- Every member of the trust family is a probability vector (total mass `α + (1-α) = 1`). -/
theorem trustPost_sum (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (hp : ∑ j, p j = 1)
    (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0) (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) (α : ℝ) :
    ∑ j, trustPost p S α j = 1 := by
  unfold trustPost
  rw [sum_split_ite]
  have hc : ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j = 1 - windowMass p S := by
    rw [← hp, ← sum_add_sum_compl S p]; unfold windowMass; ring
  have h1' : 1 - windowMass p S ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm h1)
  rw [hc]
  change α / windowMass p S * windowMass p S + _ = 1
  field_simp
  ring

/-! ## 2. Concave piecewise-linear shape -/

/-- **T7 (shape).**  `E_opt(α)` is concave in the trust level. -/
theorem trustCost_concave (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
    ConcaveOn ℝ Set.univ (trustCost p S) := by
  refine ⟨convex_univ, fun x _ y _ a b ha hb hab => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : b = 1 - a := by linarith
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]
  unfold trustCost
  rw [trustPost_affine]
  exact optCost_concave _ _ a ha (by linarith)

/-- **T7 (piecewise-linear).**  `E_opt(α)` is the minimum over all `n!` orders of the affine
functions `α ↦ α · c₁(σ) + (1 - α) · c₀(σ)`. -/
theorem trustCost_eq_inf_affine (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) :
    trustCost p S α = univ.inf' univ_nonempty (fun σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) =>
      α * probeCost (trustPost p S 1) σ + (1 - α) * probeCost (trustPost p S 0) σ) := by
  unfold trustCost optCost
  have : trustPost p S α = fun j => α * trustPost p S 1 j + (1 - α) * trustPost p S 0 j := by
    rw [← trustPost_affine]; congr 1; ring
  rw [this]
  congr 1
  ext σ
  exact probeCost_mix _ _ α σ

/-! ## 3. The uniform level is the absolute ceiling -/

/-- Scanning forwards and backwards together costs `(n+1)` times the total mass. -/
lemma probeCost_refl_add_rev (q : Fin n → ℝ) :
    probeCost q (Equiv.refl _) + probeCost q Fin.revPerm = ((n : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ j, q j := by
  unfold probeCost
  have hrev : ∑ i : Fin n, (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q (Fin.revPerm i)
      = ∑ i : Fin n, ((((Fin.revPerm i : Fin n) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q i := by
    rw [← Equiv.sum_comp Fin.revPerm (fun i => ((((Fin.revPerm i : Fin n) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q i)]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    simp [Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.rev_rev]
  rw [hrev, ← sum_add_distrib, mul_sum]
  refine sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply, Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.val_rev]
  have hi : (i : ℕ) < n := i.isLt
  rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- **Uniform ceiling.**  The Bayes-optimal cost of *any* weight vector is at most
`(n+1)/2` times its mass. -/
theorem optCost_le_uniform_level (q : Fin n → ℝ) :
    optCost q ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 * ∑ j, q j := by
  have h1 : optCost q ≤ probeCost q (Equiv.refl _) := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
  have h2 : optCost q ≤ probeCost q Fin.revPerm := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
  have := probeCost_refl_add_rev q
  linarith

/-- The uniform vector attains the ceiling: `(n+1)/2` is the global maximum of the Bayes cost
over probability vectors. -/
theorem optCost_uniform (hn : 0 < n) : optCost (fun _ : Fin n => 1 / (n : ℝ)) = ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have hb := blindCost_eq n hn
  unfold blindCost at hb
  rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone _ (Equiv.refl _) (fun _ _ _ => le_rfl), hb]

/-- **No hump exceeds the uniform level.** -/
theorem trustCost_le_uniform_level (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (hp : ∑ j, p j = 1)
    (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0) (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) (α : ℝ) :
    trustCost p S α ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have := optCost_le_uniform_level (trustPost p S α)
  rwa [trustPost_sum p S hp h0 h1, mul_one] at this

/-- **The round-39 family peaks exactly at the ceiling.**  In the uniform-given-hit model of
`Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers`, trusting the window at `α = W/M` flattens the posterior to the
uniform vector, so the Bayes cost reaches the global maximum `(M+1)/2`; no trust level exceeds it. -/
theorem hintPosterior_peak (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W < M) :
    optCost (hintPosterior M W ((W : ℝ) / M)) = ((M : ℝ) + 1) / 2 ∧
      ∀ α, optCost (hintPosterior M W α) ≤ ((M : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hW.trans hWM
  have hW' : (W : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hW.ne'
  have hMW : (M : ℝ) - W ≠ 0 := by
    have : (W : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hWM
    linarith
  refine ⟨?_, fun α => ?_⟩
  · have : hintPosterior M W ((W : ℝ) / M) = fun _ => 1 / (M : ℝ) := by
      ext j
      unfold hintPosterior
      split_ifs <;> field_simp
    rw [this, optCost_uniform (hW.trans hWM)]
  · have := optCost_le_uniform_level (hintPosterior M W α)
    rwa [hintPosterior_sum M W hW hWM α, mul_one] at this

/-! ## 4. The universal hedging hump -/

/-- Conditional mean position inside `S` under the prior. -/
noncomputable def meanIn (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ S, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j) / windowMass p S

/-- Conditional mean position outside `S` under the prior. -/
noncomputable def meanOut (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j) / (1 - windowMass p S)

/-- The committed (ascending-scan) cost is *linear* in the trust level. -/
theorem committedCost_eq (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) :
    probeCost (trustPost p S α) (Equiv.refl _) = α * meanIn p S + (1 - α) * meanOut p S := by
  unfold probeCost trustPost meanIn meanOut
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply]
  rw [← sum_add_sum_compl S]
  congr 1
  · rw [mul_div_assoc', mul_comm α, mul_div_assoc, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_
    rw [if_pos hj]; ring
  · rw [mul_div_assoc', mul_comm (1 - α), mul_div_assoc, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_
    rw [if_neg (mem_compl.mp hj)]; ring

/-- Near the calibrated trust, the posterior of a strictly decreasing prior stays decreasing. -/
lemma eventually_antitone (p : Fin n → ℝ) (hp : StrictAnti p) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    (h0 : 0 < windowMass p S) (h1 : windowMass p S < 1) :
    ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 (windowMass p S), Antitone (trustPost p S α ∘ Equiv.refl _) := by
  set P := windowMass p S with hP
  have hP1 : 1 - P ≠ 0 := by linarith
  have hcross : ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 P, ∀ i j : Fin n, i < j →
      (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p j < α / P * p i ∧ α / P * p j < (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p i := by
    refine eventually_all.2 fun i => eventually_all.2 fun j => ?_
    by_cases hij : i < j
    · have hlt := hp hij
      have tin : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => α / P * p i) (𝓝 P) (𝓝 (P / P * p i)) :=
        ((continuous_id.div_const P).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tin' : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => α / P * p j) (𝓝 P) (𝓝 (P / P * p j)) :=
        ((continuous_id.div_const P).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tout : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p i) (𝓝 P)
          (𝓝 ((1 - P) / (1 - P) * p i)) :=
        (((continuous_const.sub continuous_id).div_const _).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tout' : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p j) (𝓝 P)
          (𝓝 ((1 - P) / (1 - P) * p j)) :=
        (((continuous_const.sub continuous_id).div_const _).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have e1 : (1 - P) / (1 - P) * p j < P / P * p i := by
        rw [div_self hP1, div_self h0.ne', one_mul, one_mul]; exact hlt
      have e2 : P / P * p j < (1 - P) / (1 - P) * p i := by
        rw [div_self hP1, div_self h0.ne', one_mul, one_mul]; exact hlt
      filter_upwards [tout'.eventually_lt tin e1, tin'.eventually_lt tout e2] with α ha hb _
      exact ⟨ha, hb⟩
    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun _ h => absurd h hij
  filter_upwards [hcross, Ioo_mem_nhds h0 h1] with α hα hI
  have ha0 : 0 ≤ α / P := div_nonneg hI.1.le h0.le
  have hb0 : 0 ≤ (1 - α) / (1 - P) := div_nonneg (by linarith [hI.2]) (by linarith)
  intro i j hij
  rcases hij.lt_or_eq with hlt | heq
  · have hpij := (hp hlt).le
    obtain ⟨c1, c2⟩ := hα i j hlt
    simp only [Function.comp_apply, Equiv.refl_apply, trustPost]
    split_ifs
    · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpij ha0
    · exact c2.le
    · exact c1.le
    · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpij hb0
  · rw [heq]

/-- **T7 (hedging hump, universal form).**  For every strictly decreasing prior and every hinted
set whose conditional mean position differs from that of its complement, there is an
intermediate trust level `α ∈ (0, 1)` at which the Bayes-optimal search is strictly more
expensive than the optimal search *without* the hint. -/
theorem hedging_hump (p : Fin n → ℝ) (hp : StrictAnti p) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    (h0 : 0 < windowMass p S) (h1 : windowMass p S < 1) (hne : meanIn p S ≠ meanOut p S) :
    ∃ α, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ optCost p < trustCost p S α := by
  set P := windowMass p S with hP
  have hcal := trustPost_calibrated p S h0.ne' h1.ne
  have hB : optCost p = P * meanIn p S + (1 - P) * meanOut p S := by
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone p (Equiv.refl _) hp.antitone]
    conv_lhs => rw [← hcal]
    exact committedCost_eq p S P
  have key : ∀ α, Antitone (trustPost p S α ∘ Equiv.refl _) →
      trustCost p S α = α * meanIn p S + (1 - α) * meanOut p S := fun α hα => by
    unfold trustCost
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone _ _ hα, committedCost_eq]
  have hev := (eventually_antitone p hp S h0 h1).and (Ioo_mem_nhds h0 h1)
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
  · obtain ⟨α, ⟨hA, hI⟩, hα⟩ :=
      ((hev.filter_mono (nhdsWithin_le_nhds (s := Set.Iio P))).and self_mem_nhdsWithin).exists
    refine ⟨α, hI.1, hI.2, ?_⟩
    rw [key α hA, hB]
    have : α < P := hα
    nlinarith
  · obtain ⟨α, ⟨hA, hI⟩, hα⟩ :=
      ((hev.filter_mono (nhdsWithin_le_nhds (s := Set.Ioi P))).and self_mem_nhdsWithin).exists
    refine ⟨α, hI.1, hI.2, ?_⟩
    rw [key α hA, hB]
    have : P < α := hα
    nlinarith

/-! ## 5. The min-law, right-placed window: partial trust is the most expensive regime -/

/-- The min-law prior `P(J = j+1) = (2(M-1-j)+1)/M²` on `Fin M`. -/
noncomputable def minPrior (M : ℕ) (j : Fin M) : ℝ := minLaw M j

/-- The right-placed window: the last `W` cells. -/
def rightWindow (M W : ℕ) : Finset (Fin M) := univ.filter fun j => M - W ≤ (j : ℕ)

lemma minPrior_pos (M : ℕ) (j : Fin M) : 0 < minPrior M j := by
  unfold minPrior minLaw
  have hj : ((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast j.isLt
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by linarith [(Nat.cast_nonneg (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (j : ℕ))]
  apply div_pos _ (by positivity)
  linarith

lemma minPrior_sum (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : ∑ j, minPrior M j = 1 := by
  unfold minPrior
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun j => minLaw M j)]
  exact minLaw_sum M hM

lemma minPrior_strictAnti (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : StrictAnti (minPrior M) :=
  fun _ _ hij => minLaw_strictAnti M hM (show _ < _ from hij)

/-- Blind (no-hint) Bayes-optimal cost under the min-law: `(M+1)(2M+1)/(6M)`. -/
theorem minPrior_optCost (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) :
    optCost (minPrior M) = ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M) := by
  rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone (minPrior M) (Equiv.refl _) (minPrior_strictAnti M hM).antitone]
  unfold probeCost minPrior
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M i)]
  exact minLaw_mean M hM

/-- **T7 (min-law, right window).**  With a right-placed window of width `0 < W`, `3W ≤ M`, some
intermediate trust `α ∈ (0,1)` makes the Bayes-optimal search strictly more expensive than
(i) no hint, (ii) full distrust `α = 0`, and (iii) full trust `α = 1`. -/
theorem minLaw_right_hump (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (h3 : 3 * W ≤ M) :
    ∃ α, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ optCost (minPrior M) < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α ∧
      trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) 0 < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α ∧
      trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) 1 < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α := by
  have hM : 0 < M := by omega
  set p := minPrior M
  set S := rightWindow M W
  have hmemS : ∀ j : Fin M, j ∈ S ↔ M - W ≤ (j : ℕ) := fun j => by simp [S, rightWindow]
  have hsplit := sum_add_sum_compl S p
  rw [minPrior_sum M hM] at hsplit
  have hS0 : 0 < windowMass p S := by
    apply sum_pos (fun j _ => minPrior_pos M j)
    exact ⟨⟨M - 1, by omega⟩, (hmemS _).2 (by simp; omega)⟩
  have hSc0 : 0 < ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by
    apply sum_pos (fun j _ => minPrior_pos M j)
    exact ⟨⟨0, hM⟩, mem_compl.2 fun h => by have := (hmemS _).1 h; simp at this; omega⟩
  have hS1 : windowMass p S < 1 := by unfold windowMass; linarith
  have hc : 1 - windowMass p S = ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by unfold windowMass; linarith
  -- positions inside the window are `≥ M - W + 1`, outside `≤ M - W`
  have hin : ((M : ℝ) - W + 1) * windowMass p S ≤ ∑ j ∈ S, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j := by
    unfold windowMass; rw [mul_sum]
    refine sum_le_sum fun j hj => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (minPrior_pos M j).le
    have := (hmemS j).1 hj
    have : ((M - W : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (j : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast this
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)] at this; linarith
  have hout : ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j ≤ ((M : ℝ) - W) * ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by
    rw [mul_sum]
    refine sum_le_sum fun j hj => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (minPrior_pos M j).le
    have := mt (hmemS j).2 (mem_compl.1 hj)
    have : (((j : ℕ) + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((M - W : ℕ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega)
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)] at this; push_cast at this; linarith
  have hmIn : (M : ℝ) - W + 1 ≤ meanIn p S := by
    unfold meanIn; rw [le_div_iff₀ hS0]; exact hin
  have hmOut : meanOut p S ≤ (M : ℝ) - W := by
    unfold meanOut; rw [hc, div_le_iff₀ hSc0]; exact hout
  obtain ⟨α, hα0, hα1, hhump⟩ :=
    hedging_hump p (minPrior_strictAnti M hM) S hS0 hS1 (by intro h; linarith)
  -- the blind cost, as a mixture of the two conditional means
  have hcal := trustPost_calibrated p S hS0.ne' hS1.ne
  have hB : optCost p = windowMass p S * meanIn p S + (1 - windowMass p S) * meanOut p S := by
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone p (Equiv.refl _) (minPrior_strictAnti M hM).antitone]
    conv_lhs => rw [← hcal]
    exact committedCost_eq p S _
  refine ⟨α, hα0, hα1, hhump, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- full distrust: scanning in order costs `meanOut < blind`
    have h0le : trustCost p S 0 ≤ meanOut p S := by
      have : trustCost p S 0 ≤ probeCost (trustPost p S 0) (Equiv.refl _) := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
      rw [committedCost_eq] at this; linarith
    nlinarith
  · -- full trust: scanning backwards visits the window in the first `W` probes
    have h1le : trustCost p S 1 ≤ W := by
      have hle : trustCost p S 1 ≤ probeCost (trustPost p S 1) Fin.revPerm := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
      have hsum := trustPost_sum p S (minPrior_sum M hM) hS0.ne' hS1.ne 1
      have hpt : probeCost (trustPost p S 1) Fin.revPerm ≤ ∑ i : Fin M, (W : ℝ) * trustPost p S 1 (Fin.revPerm i) := by
        unfold probeCost
        refine sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
        by_cases hi : Fin.revPerm i ∈ S
        · have := (hmemS _).1 hi
          simp only [Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.val_rev] at this
          have hiW : (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) ≤ W := by exact_mod_cast (by omega)
          apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hiW
          unfold trustPost; rw [if_pos hi]
          exact mul_nonneg (div_nonneg zero_le_one hS0.le) (minPrior_pos M _).le
        · unfold trustPost; rw [if_neg hi]; simp
      rw [← mul_sum, Equiv.sum_comp Fin.revPerm (trustPost p S 1), hsum, mul_one] at hpt
      linarith
    have hBW : (W : ℝ) < optCost p := by
      rw [minPrior_optCost M hM]
      have hM' : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hM
      have h3' : 3 * (W : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast h3
      rw [lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
      nlinarith
    linarith

end IntervalHintsHedgingHump

order — the Bayes-optimal order inside the window (`placementCost_eq_optCost`).

## Main results
* **`placementCost_eq`** — exact placement law: with `d = M - s` (distance of the window start
  from the right end), `E = (W+1)(6d - 4W + 1) / (6(2d - W))`.
* **`placementCost_strictAnti`** — moving the window to the right strictly lowers the cost
  (`W ≥ 2`); the right-placed window is the cheapest of all placements.
* `rightCost_eq`, `right_selfSimilar` — the right window reproduces the min-law on `W` cells
  ("truncated `w` reproduces min-of-two-uniforms"): `E = (W+1)(2W+1)/(6W)`.
* **`placementSpeedup_le`** — universal ceiling: *every* placement has speedup `≤ M/W = 1/x`.
* **`placementSpeedup_tendsto`** — with `M = kW` and `d = mW`, the speedup tends to
  `k(2m-1)/(3m-2)`: `k = 1/x` for right (`m = 1`), `(2-x)/(x(3-2x))` for left (`m = k`), and
  `≈ 2/(3x)` for centered windows.
* `best_cell_right_sixteenth` — `M = 256`, right, `x = 1/16`: speedup `∈ (14.68, 14.69)`
  (reported `14.69×`).
* **`leftCommitted_eq`** and `left_crossing_eighth`, `left_crossing_sixtyfourth` — exact trusted
  committed cost for left windows; the `5.19×` crossing at `M = 256` sits in `(0.995, 0.996)` for
  `x = 1/8` and in `(0.836, 0.837)` for `x = 1/64`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Stage 1): (H1) ceiling `2/(3x)` for centered/left windows, `1/x` for right windows;
  (H2) "placement doubles what width buys"; (H3) best cell `14.69×` at right `x = 1/16`;
  (H4) `5.19×` crossing `α* = 0.832 (x=1/64) → 0.996 (x=1/8)`.
Experiment (Stage 2): exact rationals (`M = 256/512/1024`), committed window-first scan:
  `α = 1` speedups at `M = 256`: left/center/right `x = 1/64`: `34.40 / 34.47 / 45.78`;
  `x = 1/8`: `5.32 / 5.42 / 7.68`.  Crossing `5.19×`, left: `x = 1/64`: `0.8367 (256)`,
  `0.8344 (512)`, `0.8332 (1024)`; `x = 1/8`: `0.9957 (256)`, `0.9935 (512)`, `0.9923 (1024)`.
  Right `x = 1/64`: `0.8332 (256)`.  Best cell `M = 256, W = 16`: `2109384/143616 = 14.6877`.
Analysis (Stage 3): (H1) true asymptotically, and both are instances of one placement law
  `k(2m-1)/(3m-2)`.  (H2) the asymptotic right/left ratio is `(3-2x)/(2-x) → 3/2`, not `2`.
  (H3) true exactly at `M = 256`.  (H4) the `x = 1/8` value `0.996` is the left window at
  `M = 256`; the `x = 1/64` value `0.832` matches the continuum (`M → ∞`) or the right
  window, not left at `M = 256` (`0.8367`).
Critique (Stage 4): `1/x` is an exact finite-`M` ceiling over all placements, not just a limit.
-/
import Combinatorics.IntervalHintsHedgingHump

namespace IntervalHintsPlacementCeilings

open Finset Filter Topology IntervalHintsTwoNumbers IntervalHintsHedgingHump

/-! ## 1. Window sums of the min-law -/

lemma sum_minLaw_window (M s W : ℕ) :
    ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (s + r)
      = ((W : ℝ) * (2 * ((M : ℝ) - 1 - s) + 1) - W * (W - 1)) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  induction W with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [sum_range_succ, ih]; unfold minLaw; push_cast; ring

lemma sum_pos_minLaw_window (M s W : ℕ) :
    ∑ r ∈ range W, ((r : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M (s + r)
      = ((2 * ((M : ℝ) - 1 - s) + 1) * (W * (W + 1) / 2)
          - 2 * (((W : ℝ) - 1) * W * (W + 1) / 3)) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  rw [← inner_block_sum, sum_div]
  refine sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
  unfold minLaw; push_cast; ring

/-! ## 2. The placement law -/

/-- Expected probes when the oracle names the window `{s, …, s+W-1}` with certainty and the
searcher scans it in ascending order. -/
noncomputable def placementCost (M s W : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ r ∈ range W, ((r : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M (s + r)) / ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (s + r)

/-- Ascending scan is Bayes-optimal inside the window: the placement cost is the optimal cost of
the conditional distribution on the `W` window cells. -/
theorem placementCost_eq_optCost (M s W : ℕ) (hsW : s + W ≤ M) :
    placementCost M s W = optCost (fun r : Fin W =>
      minLaw M (s + r) / ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (s + r)) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos W with rfl | hW
  · simp [placementCost, optCost, probeCost]
  have hM : 0 < M := by omega
  have hZ : 0 < ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (s + r) := by
    refine sum_pos (fun r hr => ?_) ⟨0, by simp [hW]⟩
    unfold minLaw
    have : (s + r : ℕ) + 1 ≤ M := by have := mem_range.1 hr; omega
    have : ((s + r : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast this
    apply div_pos _ (by positivity); linarith
  rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone _ (Equiv.refl _)]
  · unfold placementCost probeCost
    simp only [Equiv.refl_apply]
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1) *
      (minLaw M (s + i) / ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (s + r))), sum_div]
    exact sum_congr rfl fun r _ => by ring
  · intro i j hij
    simp only [Function.comp_apply, Equiv.refl_apply]
    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hZ.le
    exact (minLaw_strictAnti M hM).antitone (Nat.add_le_add_left (show (i : ℕ) ≤ j from hij) s)

/-- **Placement law (T8).**  With `d = M - s`, the cost of the window `{s, …, s+W-1}` is
`(W+1)(6d - 4W + 1) / (6(2d - W))`. -/
theorem placementCost_eq (M s W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hsW : s + W ≤ M) :
    placementCost M s W
      = ((W : ℝ) + 1) * (6 * ((M : ℝ) - s) - 4 * W + 1) / (6 * (2 * ((M : ℝ) - s) - W)) := by
  unfold placementCost
  rw [sum_pos_minLaw_window, sum_minLaw_window]
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < M by omega)
  have hW' : (0 : ℝ) < W := by exact_mod_cast hW
  have hd : (W : ℝ) ≤ (M : ℝ) - s := by
    have : ((s + W : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast hsW
    push_cast at this; linarith
  have h1 : (2 * ((M : ℝ) - s) - W) ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  have h2 : ((W : ℝ) * (2 * ((M : ℝ) - 1 - s) + 1) - W * (W - 1)) ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  rw [div_div_div_cancel_right₀ (by positivity), div_eq_div_iff h2 (by positivity)]
  ring

/-- **Right placement is cheapest.**  For `W ≥ 2`, shifting the window to the right strictly
lowers the cost. -/
theorem placementCost_strictAnti (M s s' W : ℕ) (hW : 2 ≤ W) (hss' : s < s')
    (hs'W : s' + W ≤ M) : placementCost M s' W < placementCost M s W := by
  rw [placementCost_eq M s' W (by omega) hs'W, placementCost_eq M s W (by omega) (by omega)]
  have hW' : (2 : ℝ) ≤ W := by exact_mod_cast hW
  have hd' : (W : ℝ) ≤ (M : ℝ) - s' := by
    have : ((s' + W : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast hs'W
    push_cast at this; linarith
  have hlt : (s : ℝ) < s' := by exact_mod_cast hss'
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)]
  have key : (6 * ((M : ℝ) - s') - 4 * W + 1) * (2 * ((M : ℝ) - s) - W)
      - (6 * ((M : ℝ) - s) - 4 * W + 1) * (2 * ((M : ℝ) - s') - W)
      = -(2 * ((s' : ℝ) - s) * (W - 1)) := by ring
  have hpos : 0 < 2 * ((s' : ℝ) - s) * (W - 1) :=
    mul_pos (mul_pos two_pos (sub_pos.2 hlt)) (by linarith)
  nlinarith [mul_pos (show (0 : ℝ) < W + 1 by linarith) hpos]

/-- Cost is monotone (non-strictly) in placement for every width. -/
theorem placementCost_antitone (M s s' W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hss' : s ≤ s')
    (hs'W : s' + W ≤ M) : placementCost M s' W ≤ placementCost M s W := by
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge W 2 with h | h
  · obtain rfl : W = 1 := by omega
    rw [placementCost_eq M s' 1 hW hs'W, placementCost_eq M s 1 hW (by omega)]
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (M : ℝ) - s' := by
      have : ((s' + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast hs'W
      push_cast at this; linarith
    have h2 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (M : ℝ) - s := by
      have : (s : ℝ) ≤ s' := by exact_mod_cast hss'
      linarith
    push_cast
    rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)]
    ring_nf; rfl
  · rcases hss'.lt_or_eq with hlt | rfl
    · exact (placementCost_strictAnti M s s' W h hlt hs'W).le
    · exact le_rfl

/-- The right-placed window: cost `(W+1)(2W+1)/(6W)`. -/
theorem rightCost_eq (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W ≤ M) :
    placementCost M (M - W) W = ((W : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * W + 1) / (6 * W) := by
  rw [placementCost_eq M (M - W) W hW (by omega), Nat.cast_sub hWM]
  have hW' : (W : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hW.ne'
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (by ring_nf; positivity) (by positivity)]
  ring

/-- **Self-similarity.**  Conditioned on the right window, the target is again a
min-of-two-uniforms on the `W` window cells. -/
theorem right_selfSimilar (M W r : ℕ) (hWM : W ≤ M) (hW : 0 < W) :
    minLaw M (M - W + r) / ((W : ℝ) ^ 2 / (M : ℝ) ^ 2) = minLaw W r := by
  have hM : (M : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show M ≠ 0 by omega)
  have hW' : (W : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hW.ne'
  unfold minLaw
  push_cast [Nat.cast_sub hWM]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- The window mass of the right window is `W²/M²`. -/
theorem right_mass (M W : ℕ) (hWM : W ≤ M) :
    ∑ r ∈ range W, minLaw M (M - W + r) = (W : ℝ) ^ 2 / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  rw [sum_minLaw_window, Nat.cast_sub hWM]; congr 1; ring

/-- Blind Bayes-optimal cost under the min-law (`minPrior_optCost`). -/
noncomputable def minBlind (M : ℕ) : ℝ := ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M)

/-- Speedup of the placed perfect-coverage hint over the optimal blind scan. -/
noncomputable def placementSpeedup (M s W : ℕ) : ℝ := minBlind M / placementCost M s W

theorem minBlind_eq_optCost (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : minBlind M = optCost (minPrior M) :=
  (minPrior_optCost M hM).symm

/-- **Right-window ceiling.**  `speedup ≤ M / W = 1/x`. -/
theorem rightSpeedup_le (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W ≤ M) :
    placementSpeedup M (M - W) W ≤ (M : ℝ) / W := by
  unfold placementSpeedup minBlind
  rw [rightCost_eq M W hW hWM]
  have hW' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ W := by exact_mod_cast hW
  have hWM' : (W : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast hWM
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by linarith
  have hre : ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M) / (((W : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * W + 1) / (6 * W))
      = ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) * W / (M * ((W + 1) * (2 * W + 1))) := by
    field_simp
  rw [hre, div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)]
  have e1 : 0 ≤ 3 * (M : ℝ) * W * (M - W) := by
    have := sub_nonneg.2 hWM'; positivity
  have e2 : (W : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (by positivity) hWM' 2
  have h3 : 3 * (M : ℝ) * W ^ 2 + W ^ 2 ≤ 3 * (M : ℝ) ^ 2 * W + M ^ 2 := by nlinarith
  nlinarith

/-- **Universal placement ceiling (T8).**  Whatever the placement, a perfect-coverage window of
width `W` never buys more than `M / W = 1/x`. -/
theorem placementSpeedup_le (M s W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hsW : s + W ≤ M) :
    placementSpeedup M s W ≤ (M : ℝ) / W := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (rightSpeedup_le M W hW (by omega))
  unfold placementSpeedup
  have hpos : 0 < placementCost M (M - W) W := by
    rw [rightCost_eq M W hW (by omega)]; positivity
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < minBlind M := by
    unfold minBlind; have : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < M by omega)
    positivity
  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_left hM.le hpos
    (placementCost_antitone M s (M - W) W hW (by omega) (by omega))

/-! ## 3. The asymptotic placement law `k(2m-1)/(3m-2)` -/

/-- **Asymptotic placement law.**  With `M = kW` cells and the window starting `d = mW` cells
from the right end (`1 ≤ m ≤ k`), the speedup tends to `k(2m-1)/(3m-2)` as `W → ∞`:
`m = 1` (right) gives `k = 1/x`; `m = k` (left) gives `(2-x)/(x(3-2x))`; `m ≈ k/2` (centered)
gives `≈ 2/(3x)`. -/
theorem placementSpeedup_tendsto (k m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmk : m ≤ k) :
    Tendsto (fun W : ℕ => placementSpeedup (k * W) ((k - m) * W) W) atTop
      (𝓝 ((k : ℝ) * (2 * m - 1) / (3 * m - 2))) := by
  have hk : (1 : ℝ) ≤ k := by exact_mod_cast (le_trans hm hmk)
  have hm' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ m := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have hinv : Tendsto (fun W : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / W) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    tendsto_one_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
  have hnum : Tendsto (fun W : ℕ => ((k : ℝ) + 1 / W) * (2 * k + 1 / W) * (2 * m - 1)) atTop
      (𝓝 (((k : ℝ) + 0) * (2 * k + 0) * (2 * m - 1))) :=
    (((tendsto_const_nhds.add hinv).mul (tendsto_const_nhds.add hinv))).mul tendsto_const_nhds
  have hden : Tendsto (fun W : ℕ => (k : ℝ) * (1 + 1 / W) * ((6 * m - 4) + 1 / W)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((k : ℝ) * (1 + 0) * ((6 * m - 4) + 0))) :=
    ((tendsto_const_nhds.mul (tendsto_const_nhds.add hinv)).mul (tendsto_const_nhds.add hinv))
  have hq := hnum.div hden (by simp; constructor <;> nlinarith)
  have hval : ((k : ℝ) + 0) * (2 * k + 0) * (2 * m - 1) / ((k : ℝ) * (1 + 0) * ((6 * m - 4) + 0))
      = (k : ℝ) * (2 * m - 1) / (3 * m - 2) := by
    have : (k : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by linarith
    have : (3 * (m : ℝ) - 2) ≠ 0 := by linarith
    have : (6 * (m : ℝ) - 4) ≠ 0 := by linarith
    rw [div_eq_div_iff (by simp; constructor <;> linarith) (by linarith)]
    ring
  rw [hval] at hq
  refine hq.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop 0] with W hW
  have hW' : (0 : ℝ) < W := by exact_mod_cast hW
  have hsW : (k - m) * W + W ≤ k * W := by
    have : (k - m) * W + W = (k - m + 1) * W := by ring
    rw [this]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
  simp only [Pi.div_apply]
  unfold placementSpeedup minBlind
  rw [placementCost_eq _ _ _ hW hsW]
  have hd : ((k * W : ℕ) : ℝ) - ((k - m) * W : ℕ) = m * W := by
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub hmk]; ring
  rw [hd]
  push_cast
  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * (m * W) - W := by nlinarith
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < 6 * (m * W) - 4 * W + 1 := by nlinarith
  have hk0 : (k : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by linarith
  have hW0 : (W : ℝ) ≠ 0 := hW'.ne'
  have h3 : (6 * (m : ℝ) - 4) * W + 1 ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp

/-- Right windows (`m = 1`): the speedup tends to `k = 1/x`. -/
theorem rightSpeedup_tendsto (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    Tendsto (fun W : ℕ => placementSpeedup (k * W) ((k - 1) * W) W) atTop (𝓝 (k : ℝ)) := by
  have := placementSpeedup_tendsto k 1 le_rfl hk
  norm_num at this
  exact this

/-- In the asymptotic law, the right window is strictly better than every other placement
(`2 ≤ m`), and the left/right ratio tends to `3/2` as `k → ∞`. -/
theorem asymptotic_right_dominates (k m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    (k : ℝ) * (2 * m - 1) / (3 * m - 2) < k := by
  have hm' : (2 : ℝ) ≤ m := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have hk' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ k := by exact_mod_cast hk
  rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by linarith)]
  nlinarith

/-- **Best cell.**  `M = 256`, right window of width `16` (`x = 1/16`), perfect coverage:
speedup `2109384/143616 ∈ (14.68, 14.69)` (reported `14.69×`, ceiling `16`). -/
theorem best_cell_right_sixteenth :
    14.68 < placementSpeedup 256 240 16 ∧ placementSpeedup 256 240 16 < 14.69 := by
  have h := rightCost_eq 256 16 (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  norm_num at h
  unfold placementSpeedup minBlind
  rw [h]
  norm_num

/-! ## 4. Partial trust, left windows: the `5.19×` crossing -/

/-- The left-placed window: the first `W` cells. -/
def leftWindow (M W : ℕ) : Finset (Fin M) := univ.filter fun j => (j : ℕ) < W

lemma sum_leftWindow (M W : ℕ) (hWM : W ≤ M) (f : ℕ → ℝ) :
    ∑ j ∈ leftWindow M W, f j = ∑ r ∈ range W, f r := by
  unfold leftWindow
  rw [sum_filter, Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => if i < W then f i else 0), ← sum_filter]
  congr 1
  ext i; simp only [mem_filter, mem_range]; omega

/-- Partial-sum identity behind the min-law mean. -/
lemma minLaw_pos_partial (M N : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ range N, ((i : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M i
      = N * (N + 1) * ((2 * M + 1) / 2 - (2 * N + 1) / 3) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  have h := sum_pos_minLaw_window M 0 N
  simp only [zero_add, Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] at h
  rw [h]; ring

/-- **Exact trusted committed cost, left window.**  Trusting the left window at level `α` and
scanning in ascending order costs
`α · N_W / P_W + (1 - α)(B - N_W)/(1 - P_W)`, where `P_W = W(2M-W)/M²` is the window mass,
`N_W = W(W+1)((2M+1)/2 - (2W+1)/3)/M²` and `B = (M+1)(2M+1)/(6M)`. -/
theorem leftCommitted_eq (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W < M) (α : ℝ) :
    probeCost (trustPost (minPrior M) (leftWindow M W) α) (Equiv.refl _)
      = α * ((W * (W + 1) * ((2 * M + 1) / 2 - (2 * W + 1) / 3) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2)
              / (W * (2 * M - W) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2))
        + (1 - α) * ((((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M)
              - W * (W + 1) * ((2 * M + 1) / 2 - (2 * W + 1) / 3) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2)
              / (1 - W * (2 * M - W) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2)) := by
  have hM : 0 < M := by omega
  rw [committedCost_eq]
  have hmass : windowMass (minPrior M) (leftWindow M W) = W * (2 * M - W) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    unfold windowMass minPrior
    rw [sum_leftWindow M W hWM.le (fun j => minLaw M j)]
    unfold minLaw
    rw [← sum_div, minLaw_partial_sum]
  have hin : ∑ j ∈ leftWindow M W, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * minPrior M j
      = W * (W + 1) * ((2 * M + 1) / 2 - (2 * W + 1) / 3) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    unfold minPrior
    rw [sum_leftWindow M W hWM.le (fun j => ((j : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M j), minLaw_pos_partial]
  have htot : ∑ j : Fin M, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * minPrior M j
      = ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M) := by
    unfold minPrior
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M i)]
    exact minLaw_mean M hM
  have hout : ∑ j ∈ (leftWindow M W)ᶜ, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * minPrior M j
      = ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M)
        - W * (W + 1) * ((2 * M + 1) / 2 - (2 * W + 1) / 3) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    rw [← htot, ← hin, ← sum_add_sum_compl (leftWindow M W)]; ring
  unfold meanIn meanOut
  rw [hmass, hin, hout]

/-- Committed speedup of a trusted left window, against the optimal blind scan. -/
noncomputable def leftTrustSpeedup (M W : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  minBlind M / probeCost (trustPost (minPrior M) (leftWindow M W) α) (Equiv.refl _)

/-- **Crossing, `x = 1/8` (`M = 256`, `W = 32`).**  The `5.19×` crossing trust lies in
`(0.995, 0.996)`, and the committed speedup is strictly increasing in trust, so the crossing is
unique: the window must be *near-certain*. -/
theorem left_crossing_eighth :
    leftTrustSpeedup 256 32 0.995 < 5.19 ∧ 5.19 < leftTrustSpeedup 256 32 0.996 ∧
      StrictMono (fun α => -probeCost (trustPost (minPrior 256) (leftWindow 256 32) α)
        (Equiv.refl _)) := by
  unfold leftTrustSpeedup minBlind
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [leftCommitted_eq 256 32 (by norm_num) (by norm_num)]; norm_num
  · rw [leftCommitted_eq 256 32 (by norm_num) (by norm_num)]; norm_num

# ET-HINTS-FULL (III): the calibration gate (FACT round 40 #4, paper 148)

A hint is a *signal*: with probability `r` it fires and the searcher's posterior becomes `q`,
otherwise it becomes `q'`; truthfulness (calibration) means the prior splits as
`p = r q + (1 - r) q'`.  The round-39 model (`Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers`) uses posteriors
that are *uniform given a hit*: `q j = α / W` on the window.

## Main results
* **`uniform_hit_mass_le`** — calibration forces `r α ≤ W · p j` for every window cell `j`:
  the hit mass of a uniform-given-hit hint is capped by the *lightest* window cell.
* **`signal_value_le`** — the expected saving of any calibrated signal is at most `r (n - 1)`
  probes (value of information is linear in the firing rate).
* **`right_uniform_gate`** — under the min-law prior with a right-placed window,
  `r α ≤ W / M²`, and `α · (expected saving) < W / M = x`: a uniform-given-hit right hint saves
  fewer than `x / α` probes on average — it can never produce gains of the order of the blind
  cost `≈ M/3` (no magnitude-ordering gains).
* `right_calibrated_trust` — the calibrated trust of a right window is `x² = W²/M²`; the
  `√N`-style rightmost commitment has calibrated capacity `→ 0`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Stage 1): uniform-given-hit hints exist only at tiny coverage.
Experiment (Stage 2): `M = 512`, right `x = 1/16` (`W = 32`): cap `r α ≤ 32/512² ≈ 1.2e-4`;
  saving bound `α · saving < 1/16` probe vs blind cost `171.17`.  Left `x = 1/16`: the lightest
  window cell has mass `(2·480+1)/512² ≈ 3.7e-3`, cap `r α ≤ 0.117` — not tiny.
Analysis (Stage 3): the gate is a property of the *lightest* window cell, so it is a
  right-placement phenomenon under the min-law; for left windows the uniform family is
  merely limited (`≈ 2x(1-x)`), not negligible.
Critique (Stage 4): the bound uses only calibration and non-negativity; no symmetry or
  continuum assumption.
-/
import Combinatorics.IntervalHintsPlacementCeilings

namespace IntervalHintsCalibrationGate

open Finset IntervalHintsTwoNumbers IntervalHintsHedgingHump IntervalHintsPlacementCeilings

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- **Calibration caps the hit mass.**  If a signal firing with probability `r ≤ 1` produces a
posterior that is uniform (`α / W`) on the window `S`, then `r α / W ≤ p j` for every `j ∈ S`. -/
theorem uniform_hit_mass_le (p q q' : Fin n → ℝ) (r α : ℝ) (W : ℕ) (hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (hq' : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q' j) (hsplit : ∀ j, p j = r * q j + (1 - r) * q' j)
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) (hunif : ∀ j ∈ S, q j = α / W) :
    ∀ j ∈ S, r * α / W ≤ p j := by
  intro j hj
  rw [hsplit j, hunif j hj, mul_div_assoc]
  have := mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.2 hr1) (hq' j)
  linarith

lemma probeCost_le_card (q : Fin n → ℝ) (hq : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q j) (hs : ∑ j, q j = 1)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : probeCost q σ ≤ n := by
  unfold probeCost
  calc ∑ i : Fin n, (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q (σ i) ≤ ∑ i : Fin n, (n : ℝ) * q (σ i) := by
        refine sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (hq _)
        have : (i : ℕ) + 1 ≤ n := i.isLt
        exact_mod_cast this
    _ = n := by rw [← mul_sum, Equiv.sum_comp σ q, hs, mul_one]

lemma one_le_optCost (q : Fin n → ℝ) (hq : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q j) (hs : ∑ j, q j = 1) :
    1 ≤ optCost q := by
  unfold optCost
  refine le_inf' _ _ fun σ _ => ?_
  unfold probeCost
  calc (1 : ℝ) = ∑ i : Fin n, 1 * q (σ i) := by rw [← mul_sum, Equiv.sum_comp σ q, hs, one_mul]
    _ ≤ _ := sum_le_sum fun i _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        (by have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.cast_nonneg _; linarith) (hq _)

/-- **Value of a calibrated signal is linear in its firing rate.**  The expected saving of the
Bayes-optimal searcher who listens to the signal is at most `r (n - 1)` probes. -/
theorem signal_value_le (p q q' : Fin n → ℝ) (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r)
    (hq : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q j) (hqs : ∑ j, q j = 1) (hsplit : ∀ j, p j = r * q j + (1 - r) * q' j) :
    optCost p - (r * optCost q + (1 - r) * optCost q') ≤ r * ((n : ℝ) - 1) := by
  obtain ⟨σ, -, hσ⟩ := exists_mem_eq_inf' (univ_nonempty (α := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)))
    (fun σ => probeCost q' σ)
  have hp : p = fun j => r * q j + (1 - r) * q' j := funext hsplit
  have h1 : optCost p ≤ probeCost p σ := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
  rw [hp, probeCost_mix] at h1
  have h2 := probeCost_le_card q hq hqs σ
  have h3 := one_le_optCost q hq hqs
  have h4 : optCost q' = probeCost q' σ := hσ
  rw [hp] at *
  nlinarith

/-- **The calibration gate (min-law, right window).**  A calibrated uniform-given-hit hint on
the right window of width `W` has hit mass `r α ≤ W / M²`, and coverage times expected saving
is below `W / M = x`. -/
theorem right_uniform_gate (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W ≤ M)
    (q q' : Fin M → ℝ) (r α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (hq : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q j) (hqs : ∑ j, q j = 1) (hq' : ∀ j, 0 ≤ q' j)
    (hsplit : ∀ j, minPrior M j = r * q j + (1 - r) * q' j)
    (hunif : ∀ j ∈ rightWindow M W, q j = α / W) :
    r * α ≤ (W : ℝ) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 ∧
      α * (optCost (minPrior M) - (r * optCost q + (1 - r) * optCost q')) < (W : ℝ) / M := by
  have hM : 0 < M := by omega
  have hM' : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hM
  have hW' : (0 : ℝ) < W := by exact_mod_cast hW
  set last : Fin M := ⟨M - 1, by omega⟩
  have hlast : last ∈ rightWindow M W := by simp [rightWindow, last]; omega
  have hplast : minPrior M last = 1 / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    simp only [minPrior, minLaw, last]
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)]; push_cast; ring
  have hcap := uniform_hit_mass_le (minPrior M) q q' r α W hr1 hq' hsplit _ hunif last hlast
  rw [hplast, div_le_div_iff₀ hW' (by positivity)] at hcap
  have hra : r * α ≤ (W : ℝ) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]; linarith
  refine ⟨hra, ?_⟩
  have hval := signal_value_le (minPrior M) q q' r hr0 hq hqs hsplit
  have hM1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (M : ℝ) - 1 := by
    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast hM
    linarith
  calc α * (optCost (minPrior M) - (r * optCost q + (1 - r) * optCost q'))
      ≤ α * (r * ((M : ℝ) - 1)) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hval hα
    _ = (r * α) * ((M : ℝ) - 1) := by ring
    _ ≤ (W : ℝ) / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 * ((M : ℝ) - 1) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hra hM1
    _ < (W : ℝ) / M := by
        rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity) hM']
        nlinarith

/-- **Calibrated capacity of the rightmost commitment.**  The right window of width `W` carries
prior mass `W²/M² = x²`, so the calibrated trust of a "start at the right end" commitment
vanishes quadratically in the window fraction. -/
theorem right_calibrated_trust (M W : ℕ) (hWM : W ≤ M) :
    windowMass (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) = (W : ℝ) ^ 2 / (M : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  rw [← right_mass M W hWM]
  unfold windowMass minPrior rightWindow
  rw [sum_filter, Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => if M - W ≤ i then minLaw M i else 0),
    ← sum_filter]
  have : (range M).filter (fun i => M - W ≤ i) = (range W).map (addLeftEmbedding (M - W)) := by
    ext i
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_range, mem_map, addLeftEmbedding_apply]
    constructor
    · intro h; exact ⟨i - (M - W), by omega, by omega⟩
    · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩; omega
  rw [this, sum_map]
  rfl

end IntervalHintsCalibrationGate

/-
# ET-HINTS-FULL (I): the hedging hump (FACT round 40 #4, paper 148, theorem T7)

Continuation of `Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers` (round 39 #5).  There the hint posterior was
uniform inside and outside the window.  Here the hint is *prior-proportional*: an oracle names a
set `S` of cells and the searcher trusts it at level `α`, i.e. puts mass `α` on `S` and `1 - α`
on its complement, each spread proportionally to the prior `p`:

  `trustPost p S α j = (α / P(S)) p j`  for `j ∈ S`,   `((1-α)/(1-P(S))) p j` otherwise.

At the calibrated trust `α = P(S)` the posterior *is* the prior (`trustPost_calibrated`).  The
Bayes-optimal expected number of probes `E_opt(α) = trustCost p S α` is studied as a function of
the trust level.

## Main results
* `trustPost_affine`, `trustPost_sum` — the trust family is an affine line of probability vectors.
* **`trustCost_concave`**, `trustCost_eq_inf_affine` — `E_opt` is concave and is the minimum of the
  `n!` affine functions `α ↦ probeCost (trustPost α) σ`: concave piecewise-linear (T7, shape).
* `optCost_le_uniform_level`, **`trustCost_le_uniform_level`** — no posterior whatsoever costs more
  than the uniform level `(n+1)/2`: this is the absolute ceiling of any hump.
* `hintPosterior_peak` — in the round-39 uniform-given-hit family the hump reaches this ceiling
  exactly, at `α = W/M`.
* **`hedging_hump`** — for *every* strictly decreasing prior and *every* window whose conditional
  mean position differs from the complement's, some intermediate trust `α ∈ (0,1)` makes the
  Bayes-optimal search strictly MORE expensive than ignoring the hint (`E_opt(α) > E_opt(P(S))`).
* **`minLaw_right_hump`** — under the min-law prior `J = min(p, q)` and a right-placed window of
  width `W ≤ M/3`, partial trust is strictly worse than no hint, than full trust (`α = 1`) and
  than full distrust (`α = 0`): partial trust is the most expensive regime.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Stage 1): (H1) `E_opt(α)` is concave piecewise-linear; (H2) intermediate trust can be
  worse than *both* endpoints *and* than no hint; (H3) the hump is a min-law accident.
Experiment (Stage 2): exact rational evaluation (sorted posterior, `α` grid step `1/200`), min-law,
  `M = 512` (blind `171.17`): right `x = 1/4` peak `196.50` at `α = 0.22` (reported `196.09`);
  right `x = 1/2` `197.84`; left `x = 1/4` `186.37` at `α = 0.31`; centered `x = 1/4` `176.97`;
  right `x = 1/64` `173.76`.  Every placement shows a hump.  `M = 256`: blind `85.83`, right
  `x = 1/4` peak `98.50`.
Analysis (Stage 3): (H1) true for any prior (minimum of affine functions).  (H2) true, and
  (H3) false: the hump is universal for strictly decreasing priors — at the calibrated trust the
  greedy order is rigid, so `E_opt` is locally the *linear* committed cost, whose slope is the
  difference of the two conditional mean positions; moving trust in the uphill direction
  strictly raises the cost.  For left windows the hump sits *below* the calibrated trust.
Critique (Stage 4): the hump never exceeds `(n+1)/2` (`trustCost_le_uniform_level`, `256.5` at
  `M = 512`), so "196 vs 171" is about 29% of the way to that ceiling.  The endpoint comparison
  needs a narrow window (`3W ≤ M`); for `x = 1/2` left/right the peak still exceeds both
  endpoints numerically but this is not covered.
-/
import Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers

namespace IntervalHintsHedgingHump

open Finset Filter Topology IntervalHintsTwoNumbers

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## 1. The trust family -/

/-- Prior mass of the hinted set `S`. -/
noncomputable def windowMass (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ := ∑ j ∈ S, p j

/-- Posterior after trusting the hint "`J ∈ S`" at level `α` (prior-proportional inside and
outside `S`). -/
noncomputable def trustPost (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) (j : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  (if j ∈ S then α / windowMass p S else (1 - α) / (1 - windowMass p S)) * p j

/-- Bayes-optimal expected number of probes at trust level `α`. -/
noncomputable def trustCost (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  optCost (trustPost p S α)

/-- At the calibrated trust `α = P(S)` the posterior is the prior. -/
theorem trustPost_calibrated (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0)
    (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) : trustPost p S (windowMass p S) = p := by
  have h1' : 1 - windowMass p S ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm h1)
  ext j
  unfold trustPost
  split_ifs
  · rw [div_self h0, one_mul]
  · rw [div_self h1', one_mul]

/-- The trust family is an affine line. -/
theorem trustPost_affine (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α β t : ℝ) :
    trustPost p S (t * α + (1 - t) * β) =
      fun j => t * trustPost p S α j + (1 - t) * trustPost p S β j := by
  ext j
  unfold trustPost
  split_ifs <;> ring

lemma sum_split_ite (S : Finset (Fin n)) (a b : ℝ) (f : Fin n → ℝ) :
    ∑ j, (if j ∈ S then a else b) * f j = a * ∑ j ∈ S, f j + b * ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, f j := by
  rw [← sum_add_sum_compl S, mul_sum, mul_sum]
  congr 1
  · exact sum_congr rfl fun j hj => by rw [if_pos hj]
  · exact sum_congr rfl fun j hj => by rw [if_neg (mem_compl.mp hj)]

/-- Every member of the trust family is a probability vector (total mass `α + (1-α) = 1`). -/
theorem trustPost_sum (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (hp : ∑ j, p j = 1)
    (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0) (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) (α : ℝ) :
    ∑ j, trustPost p S α j = 1 := by
  unfold trustPost
  rw [sum_split_ite]
  have hc : ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j = 1 - windowMass p S := by
    rw [← hp, ← sum_add_sum_compl S p]; unfold windowMass; ring
  have h1' : 1 - windowMass p S ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm h1)
  rw [hc]
  change α / windowMass p S * windowMass p S + _ = 1
  field_simp
  ring

/-! ## 2. Concave piecewise-linear shape -/

/-- **T7 (shape).**  `E_opt(α)` is concave in the trust level. -/
theorem trustCost_concave (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
    ConcaveOn ℝ Set.univ (trustCost p S) := by
  refine ⟨convex_univ, fun x _ y _ a b ha hb hab => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : b = 1 - a := by linarith
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]
  unfold trustCost
  rw [trustPost_affine]
  exact optCost_concave _ _ a ha (by linarith)

/-- **T7 (piecewise-linear).**  `E_opt(α)` is the minimum over all `n!` orders of the affine
functions `α ↦ α · c₁(σ) + (1 - α) · c₀(σ)`. -/
theorem trustCost_eq_inf_affine (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) :
    trustCost p S α = univ.inf' univ_nonempty (fun σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) =>
      α * probeCost (trustPost p S 1) σ + (1 - α) * probeCost (trustPost p S 0) σ) := by
  unfold trustCost optCost
  have : trustPost p S α = fun j => α * trustPost p S 1 j + (1 - α) * trustPost p S 0 j := by
    rw [← trustPost_affine]; congr 1; ring
  rw [this]
  congr 1
  ext σ
  exact probeCost_mix _ _ α σ

/-! ## 3. The uniform level is the absolute ceiling -/

/-- Scanning forwards and backwards together costs `(n+1)` times the total mass. -/
lemma probeCost_refl_add_rev (q : Fin n → ℝ) :
    probeCost q (Equiv.refl _) + probeCost q Fin.revPerm = ((n : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ j, q j := by
  unfold probeCost
  have hrev : ∑ i : Fin n, (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q (Fin.revPerm i)
      = ∑ i : Fin n, ((((Fin.revPerm i : Fin n) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q i := by
    rw [← Equiv.sum_comp Fin.revPerm (fun i => ((((Fin.revPerm i : Fin n) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * q i)]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    simp [Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.rev_rev]
  rw [hrev, ← sum_add_distrib, mul_sum]
  refine sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply, Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.val_rev]
  have hi : (i : ℕ) < n := i.isLt
  rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- **Uniform ceiling.**  The Bayes-optimal cost of *any* weight vector is at most
`(n+1)/2` times its mass. -/
theorem optCost_le_uniform_level (q : Fin n → ℝ) :
    optCost q ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 * ∑ j, q j := by
  have h1 : optCost q ≤ probeCost q (Equiv.refl _) := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
  have h2 : optCost q ≤ probeCost q Fin.revPerm := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
  have := probeCost_refl_add_rev q
  linarith

/-- The uniform vector attains the ceiling: `(n+1)/2` is the global maximum of the Bayes cost
over probability vectors. -/
theorem optCost_uniform (hn : 0 < n) : optCost (fun _ : Fin n => 1 / (n : ℝ)) = ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have hb := blindCost_eq n hn
  unfold blindCost at hb
  rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone _ (Equiv.refl _) (fun _ _ _ => le_rfl), hb]

/-- **No hump exceeds the uniform level.** -/
theorem trustCost_le_uniform_level (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (hp : ∑ j, p j = 1)
    (h0 : windowMass p S ≠ 0) (h1 : windowMass p S ≠ 1) (α : ℝ) :
    trustCost p S α ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have := optCost_le_uniform_level (trustPost p S α)
  rwa [trustPost_sum p S hp h0 h1, mul_one] at this

/-- **The round-39 family peaks exactly at the ceiling.**  In the uniform-given-hit model of
`Logic.IntervalHintsTwoNumbers`, trusting the window at `α = W/M` flattens the posterior to the
uniform vector, so the Bayes cost reaches the global maximum `(M+1)/2`; no trust level exceeds it. -/
theorem hintPosterior_peak (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (hWM : W < M) :
    optCost (hintPosterior M W ((W : ℝ) / M)) = ((M : ℝ) + 1) / 2 ∧
      ∀ α, optCost (hintPosterior M W α) ≤ ((M : ℝ) + 1) / 2 := by
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hW.trans hWM
  have hW' : (W : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hW.ne'
  have hMW : (M : ℝ) - W ≠ 0 := by
    have : (W : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hWM
    linarith
  refine ⟨?_, fun α => ?_⟩
  · have : hintPosterior M W ((W : ℝ) / M) = fun _ => 1 / (M : ℝ) := by
      ext j
      unfold hintPosterior
      split_ifs <;> field_simp
    rw [this, optCost_uniform (hW.trans hWM)]
  · have := optCost_le_uniform_level (hintPosterior M W α)
    rwa [hintPosterior_sum M W hW hWM α, mul_one] at this

/-! ## 4. The universal hedging hump -/

/-- Conditional mean position inside `S` under the prior. -/
noncomputable def meanIn (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ S, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j) / windowMass p S

/-- Conditional mean position outside `S` under the prior. -/
noncomputable def meanOut (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j) / (1 - windowMass p S)

/-- The committed (ascending-scan) cost is *linear* in the trust level. -/
theorem committedCost_eq (p : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (α : ℝ) :
    probeCost (trustPost p S α) (Equiv.refl _) = α * meanIn p S + (1 - α) * meanOut p S := by
  unfold probeCost trustPost meanIn meanOut
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply]
  rw [← sum_add_sum_compl S]
  congr 1
  · rw [mul_div_assoc', mul_comm α, mul_div_assoc, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_
    rw [if_pos hj]; ring
  · rw [mul_div_assoc', mul_comm (1 - α), mul_div_assoc, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_
    rw [if_neg (mem_compl.mp hj)]; ring

/-- Near the calibrated trust, the posterior of a strictly decreasing prior stays decreasing. -/
lemma eventually_antitone (p : Fin n → ℝ) (hp : StrictAnti p) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    (h0 : 0 < windowMass p S) (h1 : windowMass p S < 1) :
    ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 (windowMass p S), Antitone (trustPost p S α ∘ Equiv.refl _) := by
  set P := windowMass p S with hP
  have hP1 : 1 - P ≠ 0 := by linarith
  have hcross : ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 P, ∀ i j : Fin n, i < j →
      (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p j < α / P * p i ∧ α / P * p j < (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p i := by
    refine eventually_all.2 fun i => eventually_all.2 fun j => ?_
    by_cases hij : i < j
    · have hlt := hp hij
      have tin : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => α / P * p i) (𝓝 P) (𝓝 (P / P * p i)) :=
        ((continuous_id.div_const P).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tin' : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => α / P * p j) (𝓝 P) (𝓝 (P / P * p j)) :=
        ((continuous_id.div_const P).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tout : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p i) (𝓝 P)
          (𝓝 ((1 - P) / (1 - P) * p i)) :=
        (((continuous_const.sub continuous_id).div_const _).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have tout' : Tendsto (fun α : ℝ => (1 - α) / (1 - P) * p j) (𝓝 P)
          (𝓝 ((1 - P) / (1 - P) * p j)) :=
        (((continuous_const.sub continuous_id).div_const _).mul continuous_const).tendsto P
      have e1 : (1 - P) / (1 - P) * p j < P / P * p i := by
        rw [div_self hP1, div_self h0.ne', one_mul, one_mul]; exact hlt
      have e2 : P / P * p j < (1 - P) / (1 - P) * p i := by
        rw [div_self hP1, div_self h0.ne', one_mul, one_mul]; exact hlt
      filter_upwards [tout'.eventually_lt tin e1, tin'.eventually_lt tout e2] with α ha hb _
      exact ⟨ha, hb⟩
    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun _ h => absurd h hij
  filter_upwards [hcross, Ioo_mem_nhds h0 h1] with α hα hI
  have ha0 : 0 ≤ α / P := div_nonneg hI.1.le h0.le
  have hb0 : 0 ≤ (1 - α) / (1 - P) := div_nonneg (by linarith [hI.2]) (by linarith)

  · have hpij := (hp hlt).le
    obtain ⟨c1, c2⟩ := hα i j hlt
    simp only [Function.comp_apply, Equiv.refl_apply, trustPost]
    split_ifs
    · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpij ha0
    · exact c2.le
    · exact c1.le
    · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpij hb0
  · rw [heq]

/-- **T7 (hedging hump, universal form).**  For every strictly decreasing prior and every hinted
set whose conditional mean position differs from that of its complement, there is an
intermediate trust level `α ∈ (0, 1)` at which the Bayes-optimal search is strictly more
expensive than the optimal search *without* the hint. -/
theorem hedging_hump (p : Fin n → ℝ) (hp : StrictAnti p) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    (h0 : 0 < windowMass p S) (h1 : windowMass p S < 1) (hne : meanIn p S ≠ meanOut p S) :
    ∃ α, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ optCost p < trustCost p S α := by
  set P := windowMass p S with hP
  have hcal := trustPost_calibrated p S h0.ne' h1.ne
  have hB : optCost p = P * meanIn p S + (1 - P) * meanOut p S := by
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone p (Equiv.refl _) hp.antitone]
    conv_lhs => rw [← hcal]
    exact committedCost_eq p S P
  have key : ∀ α, Antitone (trustPost p S α ∘ Equiv.refl _) →
      trustCost p S α = α * meanIn p S + (1 - α) * meanOut p S := fun α hα => by
    unfold trustCost
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone _ _ hα, committedCost_eq]
  have hev := (eventually_antitone p hp S h0 h1).and (Ioo_mem_nhds h0 h1)
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
  · obtain ⟨α, ⟨hA, hI⟩, hα⟩ :=
      ((hev.filter_mono (nhdsWithin_le_nhds (s := Set.Iio P))).and self_mem_nhdsWithin).exists
    refine ⟨α, hI.1, hI.2, ?_⟩
    rw [key α hA, hB]
    have : α < P := hα
    nlinarith
  · obtain ⟨α, ⟨hA, hI⟩, hα⟩ :=
      ((hev.filter_mono (nhdsWithin_le_nhds (s := Set.Ioi P))).and self_mem_nhdsWithin).exists
    refine ⟨α, hI.1, hI.2, ?_⟩
    rw [key α hA, hB]
    have : P < α := hα
    nlinarith

/-! ## 5. The min-law, right-placed window: partial trust is the most expensive regime -/

/-- The min-law prior `P(J = j+1) = (2(M-1-j)+1)/M²` on `Fin M`. -/
noncomputable def minPrior (M : ℕ) (j : Fin M) : ℝ := minLaw M j

/-- The right-placed window: the last `W` cells. -/
def rightWindow (M W : ℕ) : Finset (Fin M) := univ.filter fun j => M - W ≤ (j : ℕ)

lemma minPrior_pos (M : ℕ) (j : Fin M) : 0 < minPrior M j := by
  unfold minPrior minLaw
  have hj : ((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast j.isLt
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < M := by linarith [(Nat.cast_nonneg (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (j : ℕ))]
  apply div_pos _ (by positivity)
  linarith

lemma minPrior_sum (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : ∑ j, minPrior M j = 1 := by
  unfold minPrior
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun j => minLaw M j)]
  exact minLaw_sum M hM

lemma minPrior_strictAnti (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : StrictAnti (minPrior M) :=
  fun _ _ hij => minLaw_strictAnti M hM (show _ < _ from hij)

/-- Blind (no-hint) Bayes-optimal cost under the min-law: `(M+1)(2M+1)/(6M)`. -/
theorem minPrior_optCost (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) :
    optCost (minPrior M) = ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M) := by
  rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone (minPrior M) (Equiv.refl _) (minPrior_strictAnti M hM).antitone]
  unfold probeCost minPrior
  simp only [Equiv.refl_apply]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => ((i : ℝ) + 1) * minLaw M i)]
  exact minLaw_mean M hM

/-- **T7 (min-law, right window).**  With a right-placed window of width `0 < W`, `3W ≤ M`, some
intermediate trust `α ∈ (0,1)` makes the Bayes-optimal search strictly more expensive than
(i) no hint, (ii) full distrust `α = 0`, and (iii) full trust `α = 1`. -/
theorem minLaw_right_hump (M W : ℕ) (hW : 0 < W) (h3 : 3 * W ≤ M) :
    ∃ α, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ optCost (minPrior M) < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α ∧
      trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) 0 < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α ∧
      trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) 1 < trustCost (minPrior M) (rightWindow M W) α := by
  have hM : 0 < M := by omega
  set p := minPrior M
  set S := rightWindow M W
  have hmemS : ∀ j : Fin M, j ∈ S ↔ M - W ≤ (j : ℕ) := fun j => by simp [S, rightWindow]
  have hsplit := sum_add_sum_compl S p
  rw [minPrior_sum M hM] at hsplit
  have hS0 : 0 < windowMass p S := by
    apply sum_pos (fun j _ => minPrior_pos M j)
    exact ⟨⟨M - 1, by omega⟩, (hmemS _).2 (by simp; omega)⟩
  have hSc0 : 0 < ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by
    apply sum_pos (fun j _ => minPrior_pos M j)
    exact ⟨⟨0, hM⟩, mem_compl.2 fun h => by have := (hmemS _).1 h; simp at this; omega⟩
  have hS1 : windowMass p S < 1 := by unfold windowMass; linarith
  have hc : 1 - windowMass p S = ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by unfold windowMass; linarith
  -- positions inside the window are `≥ M - W + 1`, outside `≤ M - W`
  have hin : ((M : ℝ) - W + 1) * windowMass p S ≤ ∑ j ∈ S, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j := by
    unfold windowMass; rw [mul_sum]
    refine sum_le_sum fun j hj => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (minPrior_pos M j).le
    have := (hmemS j).1 hj
    have : ((M - W : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (j : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast this
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)] at this; linarith
  have hout : ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) * p j ≤ ((M : ℝ) - W) * ∑ j ∈ Sᶜ, p j := by
    rw [mul_sum]
    refine sum_le_sum fun j hj => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (minPrior_pos M j).le
    have := mt (hmemS j).2 (mem_compl.1 hj)
    have : (((j : ℕ) + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((M - W : ℕ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega)
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)] at this; push_cast at this; linarith
  have hmIn : (M : ℝ) - W + 1 ≤ meanIn p S := by
    unfold meanIn; rw [le_div_iff₀ hS0]; exact hin
  have hmOut : meanOut p S ≤ (M : ℝ) - W := by
    unfold meanOut; rw [hc, div_le_iff₀ hSc0]; exact hout
  obtain ⟨α, hα0, hα1, hhump⟩ :=
    hedging_hump p (minPrior_strictAnti M hM) S hS0 hS1 (by intro h; linarith)
  -- the blind cost, as a mixture of the two conditional means
  have hcal := trustPost_calibrated p S hS0.ne' hS1.ne
  have hB : optCost p = windowMass p S * meanIn p S + (1 - windowMass p S) * meanOut p S := by
    rw [optCost_eq_of_antitone p (Equiv.refl _) (minPrior_strictAnti M hM).antitone]
    conv_lhs => rw [← hcal]
    exact committedCost_eq p S _
  refine ⟨α, hα0, hα1, hhump, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- full distrust: scanning in order costs `meanOut < blind`
    have h0le : trustCost p S 0 ≤ meanOut p S := by
      have : trustCost p S 0 ≤ probeCost (trustPost p S 0) (Equiv.refl _) := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
      rw [committedCost_eq] at this; linarith
    nlinarith
  · -- full trust: scanning backwards visits the window in the first `W` probes
    have h1le : trustCost p S 1 ≤ W := by
      have hle : trustCost p S 1 ≤ probeCost (trustPost p S 1) Fin.revPerm := inf'_le _ (mem_univ _)
      have hsum := trustPost_sum p S (minPrior_sum M hM) hS0.ne' hS1.ne 1
      have hpt : probeCost (trustPost p S 1) Fin.revPerm ≤ ∑ i : Fin M, (W : ℝ) * trustPost p S 1 (Fin.revPerm i) := by
        unfold probeCost
        refine sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
        by_cases hi : Fin.revPerm i ∈ S
        · have := (hmemS _).1 hi
          simp only [Fin.revPerm_apply, Fin.val_rev] at this
          have hiW : (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) ≤ W := by exact_mod_cast (by omega)
          apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hiW
          unfold trustPost; rw [if_pos hi]
          exact mul_nonneg (div_nonneg zero_le_one hS0.le) (minPrior_pos M _).le
        · unfold trustPost; rw [if_neg hi]; simp
      rw [← mul_sum, Equiv.sum_comp Fin.revPerm (trustPost p S 1), hsum, mul_one] at hpt
      linarith
    have hBW : (W : ℝ) < optCost p := by
      rw [minPrior_optCost M hM]
      have hM' : (0 : ℝ) < M := by exact_mod_cast hM
      have h3' : 3 * (W : ℝ) ≤ M := by exact_mod_cast h3
      rw [lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
      nlinarith
    linarith

end IntervalHintsHedgingHump
